#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --time=06:00:00
#SBATCH --nodes=8
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=8
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=8
#SBATCH --mem=200G

# The PBS 'select' directive was translated as follows:
# select=8 -> --nodes=8
# mpiprocs=8 -> --ntasks-per-node=8
# ompthreads=8 -> --cpus-per-task=8
# ncpus=64 is implicitly requested by (ntasks-per-node * cpus-per-task) = 8 * 8 = 64
# mem=200gb -> --mem=200G

# Change to the directory where the job was submitted
cd $SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR

module purge

export OMP_NUM_THREADS=8
export MKL_NUM_THREADS=8

find . -maxdepth 1 ! -name 'run.slurm' -type f -exec rm  {} +
cp input/* .

module load CP2K/2022.1-foss-2022a

# Default CP2K 2022.1
#cp2k=/gpfs/easybuild/prod/software/CP2K/2022.1-foss-2022a/bin/cp2k.psmp

# CP2K official
#cp2k=/gpfs/home/cahart/software/cp2k-master/exe/local/cp2k.psmp
#cp2k=/gpfs/home/cahart/software/cp2k-2022.1/exe/local/cp2k.psmp
#cp2k=/gpfs/home/cahart/software/cp2k-2022.2/exe/local/cp2k.psmp

# CP2K-SMEAGOL
#cp2k=/gpfs/home/cahart/software/smeagol/cp2k-smeagol/cp2k-private/exe/local/cp2k.psmp
cp2k=/gpfs/home/cahart/software/smeagol/cp2k-smeagol/cp2k-private-external-blas/exe/local/cp2k.psmp

find . -maxdepth 1 ! -name '*slurm*' -type f -exec rm  {} +
cp input/* .

kpoints_bulk="1 1 20"
kpoints_em="1 1 1"

sed -i -e "s/KPOINTS_REPLACE/$kpoints_bulk/g"  1_bulkLR.inp
sed -i -e "s/KPOINTS_REPLACE/$kpoints_em/g"  2_dft_wfn.inp
sed -i -e "s/KPOINTS_REPLACE/$kpoints_em/g"  3_0V.inp
sed -i -e "s/KPOINTS_REPLACE/$kpoints_em/g"  4_V.inp

bulk_folder=/gpfs/home/cahart/transport/melamine/au_from-h2/leads/leads-sz_kpoints-1-1-20-cu
cp $bulk_folder/*bulk* .
wait

#dft_folder=/gpfs/home/cahart/transport/melamine/au_size-6-6-6/capacitor/dft_kpoints-1-1-20
#cp $dft_folder/*dft* .
#wait

HLB="$(grep '0.0000000000' bulk-VH_AV.dat | head -1 | awk '{print $2}')"
sed -i -e "s/HLB_REPLACE/${HLB}/g"  3_0V.inp

# Using srun is the Slurm-native way to launch parallel jobs.
srun $cp2k -i 3_0V.inp -o log_3_0V.out

V=1.0
echo $V
mv 4_V.inp 4_${V}V.inp
sed -i -e "s/PROJECT_REPLACE/${V}V/g" 4_${V}V.inp
sed -i -e "s/HLB_REPLACE/${HLB}/g"  4_${V}V.inp
sed -i -e "s/V_REPLACE/${V}/g"  4_${V}V.inp

# Using srun is the Slurm-native way to launch parallel jobs.
srun $cp2k -i 4_${V}V.inp -o log_4_${V}V.out

issues: A destructive `find ... -exec rm ...` command is run twice. The second instance will delete the output files (e.g., `log_3_0V.out`) and modified input files from the first `srun` command before the second `srun` command begins, which is likely not the intended behavior.

The script loads a specific CP2K module (`module load CP2K/2022.1-foss-2022a`) but then ignores it by using a hardcoded, absolute path to a different executable (`cp2k=/gpfs/home/cahart/software/smeagol/...`). This makes the script less portable and the `module load` command misleading.
The `wait` command after the `cp` command is unnecessary, as `cp` is a synchronous operation and the script will wait for it to complete by default.
The initial cleanup command `find . -maxdepth 1 ! -name 'run.slurm' ...` is very specific and aggressive. If the submission script is named anything other than 'run.slurm', it will be deleted.
